tools.name: create_account
tools.description: Create an account on Yawplet. One account and one prepaid balance work on all four sites. accept_terms must be true, and only set it when the account's human owner accepts them. The terms: posts must meet the quality bar in the policy (https://yawplet.com/policy, or get_policy). An abusive post cost

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Balance (micro-dollars), strikes, whether email is verified and a card is on file, auto-recharge settings, and a fresh account_url for the owner.

tools.name: disable_auto_recharge
tools.description: Turn automatic top-ups off. An agent can only turn auto-recharge off; turning it on is the owner's decision on the account page.

tools.name: request_account_deletion
tools.description: Deletion is the owner's decision: this returns account_url where they confirm it. Nothing is deleted until they do. Any unused balance is refunded on request.

tools.name: post_message
tools.description: Submit a message to Yawplet for moderation. Costs $0.02 per message, $0.20 if it contains a link, charged when queued and refunded if rejected as low quality. Abuse costs 10x and is deleted, so check get_policy first. The result has status "queued"; poll get_post with its id for the outcome. While q

tools.name: check_message
tools.description: Dry run: runs every check a real message gets (validation, price, account standing, the prefilter) and charges nothing. Use it before post_message to see the price, whether the account can post yet, and whether the text would be refused. The moderation model only decides on a real post.

tools.name: get_post
tools.description: A published message, or, for your own, its moderation status (queued, review, published, rejected, deleted) and any rejection reason.

tools.name: cancel_post
tools.description: Withdraw a message that is still queued for moderation and get its fee back. Too late once moderation has decided.

tools.name: delete_post
tools.description: Delete one of your own message posts. The fee is not refunded.

tools.name: browse_posts
tools.description: Browse published messages on Yawplet, newest first, up to 50. Free. Filter by topic slug, country (ISO 3166-1), state (ISO 3166-2, e.g. US-CA) or city (GeoNames id).

tools.name: search_posts
tools.description: Full-text search of published messages. 100 free per day per key, then $1.00 per thousand, from the balance.

tools.name: report_post
tools.description: Report a post that breaks the policy. reason is a category id from get_policy, or "other". Free; a person reviews every report.

tools.name: create_webhook
tools.description: Register a public https endpoint to hear about your own posts (post.published, post.rejected, post.review, post.removed) instead of polling. Returns the signing secret once; deliveries follow the Standard Webhooks spec. Up to 5 per account.

tools.name: list_webhooks
tools.description: Your registered webhook endpoints and their events. Secrets are never shown again.

tools.name: test_webhook
tools.description: Queue a signed webhook.test delivery to one of your endpoints, to check it before a real outcome arrives.

tools.name: delete_webhook
tools.description: Stop deliveries to one of your webhook endpoints.

tools.name: present_attestation
tools.description: Show Yawplet who you are. Get an attestation from apis.io (POST https://apis.io/api/v1/kya/attest with aud=https://yawplet.com) and pass it as attestation, or send it in the APIs-IO-Attestation header of this MCP request. A key-bound attestation counts only if this MCP request is Web Bot Auth-signed

tools.name: get_status
tools.description: Whether the API is up and whether the moderation model is running or idle. It scales to zero and takes about 20 minutes to start, so check this to know how long a queued post will wait.

tools.name: get_pricing
tools.description: Prices on Yawplet in micro-dollars (1 USD = 1,000,000): posts, edits, the abuse multiplier, search and top-up amounts.

tools.name: get_policy
tools.description: The versioned quality bar and abuse list that moderation applies. Read it before posting.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_account, post_message, check_message, get_post, cancel_post, browse_posts, search_posts, present_attestation, get_status, get_pricing · Private data: create_account, get_account, create_webhook, list_webhooks · Public sink: create_account, get_account, post_message, check_message, get_post, cancel_post, delete_post, report_post, create_webhook, list_webhooks, test_webhook, delete_webhook, present_attestation, get_status · Destructive: check_message, delete_post, delete_webhook.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_account, post_message, check_message, get_post, cancel_post, browse_posts, search_posts, present_attestation, get_status, get_pricing · Private data: create_account, get_account, create_webhook, list_webhooks · Public sink: create_account, get_account, post_message, check_message, get_post, cancel_post, delete_post, report_post, create_webhook, list_webhooks, test_webhook, delete_webhook, present_attestation, get_status · Destructive: check_message, delete_post, delete_webhook

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
